bins.desc: Windows Sandbox command-line interface. Creates, lists, controls, and executes commands inside Windows Sandbox sessions from the host CLI.

fns.code:
wsb start --config "<Configuration><LogonCommand><Command>{CMD}</Command></LogonCommand></Configuration>"
wsb exec -r System --id YOUR_ID
fns.c: Executes the given command in a Windows Sandbox from an inline XML configuration with an embedded `<LogonCommand>`, leaving no `.wsb` file on disk. Note: `<LogonCommand>` only fires once `WDAGUtilityAccount` actually logs in, which only happens after an RDP session is established via `wsb connect`, so this pattern opens a visible Sandbox window.
fns.use: Fileless execution of arbitrary commands in an EDR-free environment whose host-side process tree is masked by the Sandbox client binaries.

fns.code:
wsb start --config "<Configuration><MappedFolders><MappedFolder><HostFolder>{PATH_ABSOLUTE:folder}</HostFolder><ReadOnly>false</ReadOnly></MappedFolder></MappedFolders></Configuration>"
wsb exec -r System --id YOUR_ID -c "cmd.exe /c copy C:\users\WDAGUtilityAccount\Desktop\Temp\{PATH} {PATH}"
fns.c: Allows the specified folder to be accessible from within the Windows Sandbox, mounted under `C:\users\WDAGUtilityAccount\Desktop` with the same folder name as the source folder. This allows, for example, for copying payloads from the host system into the sandbox (seen here), copying payloads from the sandbox back to the host system, or for accessing arbitrary host system files by the sandbox.
fns.use: Fileless execution of arbitrary commands in an EDR-free environment, with access to files on the host system, while the host-side process tree is masked by the Sandbox client binaries.

fns.code:
wsb start
wsb share --id YOUR_ID -f {PATH_ABSOLUTE:folder} -s c:\SOME_FOLDER --allow-write
wsb exec -r System --id YOUR_ID -c "cmd.exe /c copy {PATH_ABSOLUTE} c:\SOME_FOLDER"
fns.c: Allows the specified folder to be accessible from within the Windows Sandbox, mounted at `c:\SOME_FOLDER`. This allows, for example, for copying payloads from the host system into the sandbox, copying payloads from the sandbox back to the host system (seen here), or for accessing arbitrary host system files by the sandbox.
fns.use: Fileless execution of arbitrary commands in an EDR-free environment, with access to files on the host system, while the host-side process tree is masked by the Sandbox client binaries.
